issues.description: The organisation-scope test (tests/test_api.py:97, test_rest_rule_counts_only_own_organisations_shifts) cannot fail on a scope regression. Riverside worker 101 has no shifts in Northfield, so the test still gets 200 even if shifts_of_worker stopped filtering on org_id. In practice the scope is enforced by the code (assignments.py:30-32 calls Scope.shifts_of_worker, and data.py:68 filters on org_id) and by tests/test_isolation.py, not by this test.
issues.resolution: Add a test whose result depends on the org filter. For example, insert a shift for worker 101 with a Northfield org_id that would leave under 11 hours of rest before Riverside shift 102 (a test fixture, not a schema change), then assert the Riverside manager's assign still returns 200. Or unit-test assignments.candidates()/problem_for() with a Scope for one organisation and a shift that belongs to another organisation.

issues.description: assignments.candidates() (assignments.py:42-47) runs one shifts_of_worker query per candidate for every open shift each time the board renders (N×M queries). The spec notes this is acceptable at demo scale.
issues.resolution: Load the organisation's assigned shifts once per board render (one scoped query grouped by worker_id) and pass them into candidates().

issues.description: tests/test_api.py:97 test_rest_rule_counts_only_own_organisations_shifts cannot fail if organisation scoping breaks. Riverside worker 101 (Elena Novak) is never assigned to any Northfield shift in seed.py, so an unscoped shifts_of_worker() would return the same rows and the test would still get 200. The code is correctly scoped (assignments.py:30-32 calls Scope.shifts_of_worker, data.py:67-70 filters org_id), so only the test is weak.
issues.resolution: Make the test fail without org scoping. One way: insert, in the test only, a Northfield-org shift row with worker_id=101 that ends less than 11 hours before Riverside shift 102 starts, then assert the Riverside manager still gets 200. Another way: call assignments.candidates(Scope(riverside), shift_102) and assert Elena Novak's unavailable is None in that setup.

issues.description: assignments.py:45-47 candidates() runs one organisation-scoped shifts_of_worker query per role-matching worker for every open shift on the board (N×M queries). The spec notes this is acceptable at demo scale.
issues.resolution: If the board grows, load the organisation's assigned shifts once in app.shifts() (through Scope) and pass them, grouped by worker_id, into candidates().

combined_verdict.summary: The change adds an 11-hour rest rule to rules.py (MIN_REST, NEEDS_REST, too_little_rest, lacks_rest), checked last in assignment_problem(). Because both the board and the API go through assignments.assign(), they refuse the same way, and the API answers 409 with {"error": "Needs 11 hours rest"}. assignments.candidates() reads each worker's shifts only through the organisation-scoped Scope.shifts_of_worker(), and templates/shifts.html shows unavailable workers as disabled options labelled "Name — Needs 11 hours rest". Every acceptance criterion is met: the logs show pytest at 58 passed and isolation at 16 passed, the e2e run passed all 11 steps, and screenshots 03/04 and keyframes 02/03 show Amara Jones and Sam Okafor greyed out with the reason. No protected path changed and no existing test expectation was loosened. | The change adds a pure 11-hour rest rule to rules.py (MIN_REST, NEEDS_REST, too_little_rest, lacks_rest), checked after the overlap rule in assignment_problem. Because assignments.assign() already serves both the board form and POST /api/shifts/<id>/assign, the two refuse in the same way (409, "Needs 11 hours rest"). assignments.candidates() uses the same rule on organisation-scoped shifts to mark workers unavailable, and templates/shifts.html shows them as disabled options with the reason. It matches every acceptance criterion and touches no protected path. The logs show 58/58 pytest, 16/16 isolation tests and a passing 11-step e2e run. Screenshots 03 and 04 and keyframes session-02 and session-03 show 'Amara Jones — Needs 11 hours rest' and 'Sam Okafor — Needs 11 hours rest' greyed out in the dropdowns, and the existing assign and expired-registration flows still work.
